passage:
Avni: They made me project lead today. I keep thinking they'll find out I don't know what I'm doing.
Jomon: You built the whole payment module.
Avni: With a lot of googling and Priya fixing my bugs.
Jomon: Everyone googles. You know that, right?
Avni: 😔 I know. It doesn't feel true at 1 a.m.
Jomon: Do you have a list of what you shipped this year?
Avni: There's a list?
Jomon: Make one. And ask your manager for feedback. A real question, like "what should I do better?"
Avni: Scary. But okay. I'll ask on Monday.
Jomon: And it's fine to say "I don't know yet" in meetings.
Avni: 🙂 Fine. Thank you.

qa.a: Avni built the whole payment module.

qa.q: What is Avni afraid of after being made project lead?
qa.a: Avni fears being found out as not knowing what Avni is doing, a fear that feels strongest at 1 a.m.

qa.q: What steps does Jomon suggest to handle the feeling?
qa.a: Keep a list of what Avni shipped this year, ask the manager a real question about what to do better, and be willing to say "I don't know yet" in meetings.

qa.q: How does Jomon seem to see Avni's abilities?
qa.a: Jomon sees real achievement, pointing to the payment module and noting that everyone googles, and treats the doubt as common rather than as proof of fraud.

grounding: Success brings impostor fear; a friend points to the record of achievements, suggests asking for feedback and says not-knowing is fine.

passage:
Indu: I got it. Project lead for the whole Bangalore office
Jasleen: WHAT 🎉🎉 I told you!!
Indu: I'm terrified
Indu: I keep thinking they made a mistake. that in the first meeting everyone will see I don't know anything
Jasleen: you've literally run three projects on time
Indu: that was luck. and good teams
Jasleen: that's what everyone who's good says
Jasleen: my boss told me she felt like a fraud for her first year as director
Indu: really?
Jasleen: really. it's super common
Jasleen: do this. write down everything you've done that worked. keep it in your phone
Indu: ok. and?
Jasleen: ask your manager what they want to see in the first 3 months. and it's fine to say "I don't know yet, I'll find out"
Indu: I can do that
Indu: still scared though
Jasleen: scared and doing it anyway 💪

qa.a: Project lead for the whole Bangalore office.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling about the new role?
qa.a: Indu felt terrified, worried they had made a mistake and that everyone would see Indu didn't know anything.

qa.q: What steps did Jasleen suggest, and why do they help?
qa.a: Writing down past successes, asking the manager for expectations, and saying "I don't know yet" when needed, which builds real confidence without pretending.

qa.q: How does Jasleen see Indu's fear?
qa.a: Jasleen sees it as the common fear capable people feel, like Jasleen's boss did, not a sign that Indu isn't good enough.

grounding: The chat shows someone gripped by fear of being found out after a success, learning it is common, and deciding to keep a record of achievements, ask for feedback and admit what they do not yet know.

passage:
Preeti was the first woman agriculture officer the block office near Satara had ever had. On her first day, farmers lined up to ask her about soil tests, seed subsidies and a strange fungus on their grapes.

She answered what she could. Inside, a voice kept whispering: they'll find out you only topped the exam. You've never grown anything.

That evening, her colleague Aditi found her staring at a pile of files. "Tired?"

"Scared," Preeti admitted. "I feel like a fraud. The farmers know more than me."

Aditi laughed gently. "They know their fields. You know the science. And everyone feels like this in their first year. I did."

"So what do I do?"

"Keep a notebook of what you get right. When you don't know, say so and find out. And spend a day on a farm every week. Learn from them."

The next morning, Preeti told a farmer, "I don't know that fungus yet. I'll ask the university and come to your field on Thursday." He nodded, satisfied.

qa.q: What was strange on the farmers' grapes?
What was Preeti feeling as she stared at the files?
qa.a: She felt scared and like a fraud, worried the farmers knew more than her.

qa.q: What did Aditi suggest, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Keeping a notebook of successes, admitting when she doesn't know and finding out, and learning on farms weekly, which builds real skill without pretending.

qa.q: How might the farmer see Preeti's honest answer?
qa.a: The farmer seems satisfied and may trust her more because she promised to find out rather than guessing.

grounding: The passage shows a young officer feeling like an impostor after success, learning many feel this, keeping a record, admitting what she doesn't know and continuing to learn.
